name: Raudkorna
description:
A strange affliction has descended upon the forests. Although the trees do not die outright, the leaves now seem to burn continually with the color of flame. The entire landscape seems newly alive with elemental energy. Every year the blight seems to creep a few miles outward, and more residents find the power of flame within themselves.

A cult of worship of The Unknown, an entity vaguely credited with the change, has arisen quickly among the hamlets and vills of the region, spreading like wildfire to the edges of the tree-turning, and now grasping beyond. The Cult initially served to hold communities together as the world changed around them, but now it binds them in arcane duties, with tithing and with missionary work quotas.

Perhaps due to those latter efforts or perhaps due to some magnetism of the region itself, newcomers have flocked into the region, settling in the flametouched recesses of what is now known as the Raudkorna, or red horn, and begin to notice changes in themselves...

Determining the nature of The Unknown

When a player character gains the Cultist or Pray to the Unknown ability, you must determine the nature of The Unknown. Choose a player to be the keeper of this knowledge. That player flips a coin:

  • Tails means that The Unknown does not exist, and the Cult of The Unknown is founded on a lie. The goals and actions of The Cult - its members and leadership - are entirely their own.

  • Heads means that The Unknown does exist. The player who flipped the coin must answer these questions: What is The Unknown? What is the source of its power? What are its goals?

The player who performed the coin flip is responsible for recording this information in secret and sharing it with each GM who runs a Quest that includes the player character with the the Cultist or Pray to the Unknown ability.

hooks.name: High Tithe
hooks.description: A rogue priest of the Cult of the Unknown has raised tithes to unprecedented rates in a remote parish. Those unable or unwilling to pay up have been thrown in jail or chased out of town. A small band of defiant citizens has fled, seeking help in deposing the priest or otherwise restoring reason to their village and their faith.
hooks.gmNotes:
Our Heroes will need to determine the best way to get into the area of the village without attracting the attention of the priest's many enforcers - village bullies armed with magical weapons carved from flametouched trees.

Should Our Heroes gain access to the priest's quarters in the church, they should find a trapdoor leading to a secret chamber below the church, where the priest has been putting the tithed goods to use.

What have they been doing with these good? What are they feeding? Some spirit of flame? Themselves, and thus becoming a powerful monster? The Unknown itself?

hooks.name: Hot on the Trail
hooks.description: A merchant guild needs to get an important shipment of goods through an area of the forest that has recently been subject to unpredictable earthquakes and fires. The path will be narrow and the convoy will be long, slow and vulnerable, but the guild is paying top dollar.
hooks.gmNotes:
This adventure is an opportunity to explore the ways in which the "Blight" is transforming the natural world of the region. Our Heroes and a very slow, very stupid, easily-spooked caravan of ox-drawn carts and carriages must navigate shifting patterns of "fires," which appear to just be a further expression of the turning of the trees, moving beyond the appearance of flame in their branches to actual flame that burns but does not consume the branches.

The narrow path along the ridgeline is cut off by a newly-formed fissure. Perhaps the only way to proceed is through fiery caves. Perhaps fire or ash spirits block the way.

What does all this say about the force or forces causing the change? Is it a natural phenomenon or is there a will moving it?

Throw a small group of passenger NPCs into the mix with competing motivations for some extra contour.

hooks.name: Trouble in Brimsholler
hooks.description: People have been going missing in the remote hamlet of Brimsholler. Some have been walking into the woods at night, never returning. At the same time, ashen spirits have been making assaults on the outlying buildings, consuming them in flame, the hissing smoke seeming to intone "join us."
hooks.gmNotes:
The spirits are of course the missing persons. They have been lured into the woods and turned into emissaries of the force that is changing the Raudkorna - whatever that might be.

Optionally, there can be a tension of doctrine among the Cultist villagers: is this spiritual state a corruption of faith or some new, purer form of devotion?

Whatever the truths, the fact remains that the people of the town grow fewer every night, and the ring of smoldering ruins moves toward the center of town each day. If Our Heroes are not to become ash spirits themselves, they'll need to confront this growing army of fire-wielding spirits.
